slides.text:
**One developer says cheap open models are now frontier-grade. I think that's half right.**

DeepSeek 4.1 Flash is the latest test case.

It kicked off one of the biggest debates among developers this week.

panel.small: on one blog post about a cheap model

slides.text:
The claim: DeepSeek 4.1 Flash behaves like a frontier model, at a fraction of the cost.

The article's author says frontier labs should be "freaking out" because China is closing the gap.

His daily sessions cost under $2, versus $20 to $100+ on frontier subscriptions.

He's right that "good enough" changes how people work.

Developers in the discussion confirmed running all-day agent sessions on Flash for a dollar or two.

At that price, you stop thinking twice before handing a task to the model.

Where it breaks: most people aren't comparing real costs.

One developer in the discussion tried the cheapest provider on the open market and burned $50 in days, a quarter of a full frontier subscription's usage.

**The savings are mostly subsidized subscriptions, not a true price gap.**
bullets: Subsidized plans hide real API pricing.
Quality claims are subjective and task-specific.
"A month or two behind" is doing a lot of work.

slides.text: The strongest pushback came from another developer in the discussion, directly disputing the article's timeline.

panel.big: "It's plausible that open models are 6-12 months behind... leading labs have nothing to fear."

slides.text:
What to do Monday: measure your own tasks instead of going on vibes.

Run your real workload through a cheap and a frontier model, both at list price.

Then use the cheap one for bulk work and keep a frontier model for review and planning.

Are "good enough" models already running your bulk work, or are you still all-in on frontier?

**Tell me where you land,** and save this before you pick your next default model.
